candidates.name: Spain Square
candidates.content: The largest square in the city, with an artificial lake fountain by Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron in its centre. It was constructed at the original location of the Castle of San Cristóbal in 1929.

candidates.name: Museum of Nature and Archeology
candidates.alt: Museo de la Naturaleza y Arqueología
candidates.content: Considered one of the best repositories of Pre-Castilian objects on the Canary Islands, with significant paleontological, botanical, entomological, and marine and terrestrial vertebrate collections. It holds the largest collection

candidates.name: Palmetum
candidates.price: Adults , children , under 2 years old free
candidates.content: Botanical garden with an area of 120 000 m² specialized in palms, set on an artificial hill overlooking the ocean. The garden includes a large system of streams, ponds, and waterfalls, as well as a museum dedicated to palms and a

candidates.name: Church of St. Francis of Assisi
candidates.alt: Iglesia de San Francisco de Asís
candidates.content: The second most important church in the city, after the Church of the Conception, completed in 1680 and notable for the large number of artworks inside. It is a good example of Baroque architecture on the Canary Islands.

candidates.name: Castle of San Cristóbal
candidates.content: The first fortification of significance on Tenerife, intended as defensive stronghold for the Santa Cruz Bay, constructed between 1575 and 1577 to protect the city against pirates. From the 20th century it lost its significance as

candidates.name: Canarian Military History Museum
candidates.content: Military history museum in the north of the city, housed in Fort Almeyda, a fortress built in 1859 to house artillery pieces to protect the vulnerable side of Santa Cruz against English invaders threatening the coast since 1797 un

candidates.name: Museum of Fine Arts
candidates.alt: Museo Municipal de Bellas Artes de Santa Cruz de Tenerife
candidates.content: Museum founded in 1840 when the city took the initiative to store flags from the Battle of Cape St Vincent in a permanent location. The classic style building was established in 1929 by architect Eladio Laredo, and decorated with

candidates.name: Tenerife Space of Arts
candidates.content: Cultural space and modern arts museum opened in 2008, with a permanent exhibition of the works of Óscar Domínguez.

candidates.name: Museo Arqueológico
candidates.content: Has a large collection of indigenous Guanche artifacts, with a focus on pottery.

candidates.name: Castillo de San Felipe
candidates.content: A small defensive fortress built in the early 17th century to defend the town against pirates. After being completely renovated in the late 20th century, it is now used as a venue for concerts and art exhibits.

candidates.name: Iglesia de San Francisco
candidates.content: Likely the oldest building in Puerto de la Cruz, the church was built between 1599 and 1608 and was attached to a no-longer extant Franciscan monastery.

candidates.name: Ermita de San Telmo
candidates.content: The small chapel was built in 1780 and dedicated to the patron saint of seafarers. After being partly destroyed by flooding in 1826 the chapel was rebuilt, and fully restored several years ago. Of special note is the interior Mude

candidates.name: Castle of St John the Baptist
Photo Center Tenerife Island
candidates.content: Opened in 1989, the centre owns a studio and photo lab, a conference room, and specialized library with more than 3500 books and files.

candidates.name: García Sanabria Park
candidates.content: Public park inaugurated in 1926, laid out as a large garden with fountains and architecture. It is the largest urban park in the Canarias with an area of 67 230 m². The most important eye catcher is the park's floral clock, manufa

candidates.name: Museum of Fishery
candidates.content: A small museum with ship models.

candidates.name: Loro Parque
candidates.content: A world class zoo that originally started out as a humble parrot park (hence the name). It features the usual big cats, apes, giant turtles, an aquarium, ... as well as the island's only roller coaster. Shows present parrots, dolp

candidates.name: Jardín de Aclimatación de la Orotava
candidates.content: Established in 1788 to acclimatize specimens brought back from the New World on their way to mainland Spain, the small Botanical Gardens have an interesting selection of tropical trees and shrubs. Even if you're not interested, it

candidates.name: Jardín de Orquideas Sitio Litre
candidates.content: The lovely English-style garden of an 18th-century mansion features a large collection of orchids along with bonsai trees and a dragon tree. Famous past visitors have included Sir Richard Burton as well as Agatha Christie, who was

candidates.name: Auditorio de Tenerife
candidates.content: Auditorium designed by architect Santiago Calatrava, on the shore of the Atlantic Ocean. Constructed between 1997 and 2003, the design is framed within the tenets of late-modern architecture of the late 20th century, and regarded

candidates.name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo Eduardo Westerdahl
candidates.alt: MACEW / Eduardo Westerdahl Museum of Contemporary Art
candidates.content: It was established in 1953 as Spain's first contempoary art museum, in the former Royal Customs House. It has a good collection of modern works by Canary Island artists.

candidates.name: Plaza Charco
candidates.content: Historic central square of Puerto de la Cruz with a fountain in the middle, and lots of shops, bars, and restaurants around it.

candidates.name: Batería de Santa Bárbara
candidates.content: This defensive fortification was built in the mid-18th century to protect the city from pirates.

candidates.name: Parque Taoro
candidates.content: Park with fountains, waterfalls, and plenty of benches to take a rest in the shade while making your way up the slopes of Puerto de la Cruz. Nice view of the city center.

candidates.name: Lago Martiánez
candidates.price: Adult €5.50, child under 10 €2.50; price includes sunbeds
candidates.content: A fantastic, post-modern swimming and sunbathing complex designed by the famous Lanzaroteno architect Cesar Manrique. It's a bit concretey by modern standards but is still an awesome paradise which costs hardly anything to enter f

candidates.name: Parque Marítimo César Manrique
candidates.content: Water park designed by architect César Manrique, covering an area of 22 000 m², and aims to recreate a natural environment with volcanic rocks, palm trees, and ornamental plants. It has pools with sea water, artificial waterfalls,

candidates.name: Carnival of Santa Cruz de Tenerife
candidates.content: The carnival is the second biggest event of its kind (after the Rio de Janeiro Carneval). The historical event is held every February, and attracts around a million of visitors.

candidates.name: Vinoteca Con Pasión
candidates.content: Gastropub and tapas bar with higher quality food.

candidates.name: Mesón Los Gemelos
candidates.content: Popular with both locals and tourists, this restaurant serves traditional Canarian cuisine in a pleasant setting with friendly service. On weekends the queues to get in can be very long, so reservations are recommended.

candidates.name: Tasca Bodega Candido
candidates.content: Tasca with typical Canarian food. Well presented. Abundant tapas. The ropa vieja with shredded meat is highly recommended. The place is very cosy. Fast service.

candidates.name: bodegon el puntero
candidates.content: Small, authentic restaurant.' Fresh seafood and fish. Very tasty. Good atmosphere. Very friendly waiters. Locals eat here on a daily basis. They have more than 40 years of experience.

candidates.name: Gonzalo's Bar Restaurant
candidates.content: Tender grilled meat. Nice grilled entrecôte. Calm backstreet seating. The escape from the sun in the shade is appreciated. The fish tartare and shrimp tempura are both very good.

candidates.name: El Porron Tasca Andaluza
candidates.content: Often regarded as the best restaurant of Santa Cruz, it specializes in a mix of Andalusian specialties and local Canarian cuisine. Great food, but relatively pricey.

candidates.name: El Taller de Seve Diaz
candidates.content: Traditional Canarian food masterfully prepared by chef Seve and his team. They have a large selection of wines to choose from.

candidates.name: Restaurante La Cayena
candidates.content: Good place to taste homemade menus. Their menus are healthy, they change them every day, always trying to make innovative dishes..

candidates.name: PizzArte
candidates.content: Very good pizzas, salads, and very friendly service. Modest and quiet inside. Also working late in the evening and the service is good.

candidates.name: Taberna del Puerto
candidates.content: Traditional restaurant. Great food and wine. The staff is friendly and professional. Cozy atmosphere. Service may be a bit slow.

candidates.name: La Albahaca
candidates.content: Takeaway, homemade food. The roasted chickens have a very good taste. Nice service.

candidates.name: Etéreo by Pedro Nel
candidates.content: Upscale Spanish restaurant with a serious price tag. The food is excellent, and accompanied by a rich selection of local and European wines.

candidates.name: Picatostes
candidates.content: Small place with great food. The lamb is nice. Well-chosen natural products and a varied menu of food and wine. The appetizer is offered as a courtesy on the house.

candidates.name: La Recova
candidates.alt: Mercado de Nuestra Señora de África
candidates.content: Covered market in Neocolonial style, built in 1943 to accommodate the needs of the growing city after the old market on the other side of the Ravine of the Saints had become too small. It played an important role in the distributi

candidates.name: Centro Comercial Meridiano
candidates.content: Shopping mall with free toilets and a Carrefour supermarket to stock up on snacks and drinks.

candidates.name: Mercado Municipal
candidates.content: The city's main market has 30 stalls; services and non-food related goods are located on the ground floor, and food items are sold on the first floor. There is also an Alteza supermarket in the building.

candidates.name: Centro Comercial las Pirámides de Martiánez
candidates.content: The main shopping centre has a number of shops and restaurants, including a Mercadona supermarket.

december.text: – Popular with tourists and locals, and great hub for hiking adventures into the Los Gigantes canyons and tunnels, Chinyero and the almond flower trail from Santiago del Teide, Teno Rural Park (with hikes to Punta de Teno from Teno Alto), and Masca

In summer (June to September), temperatures range between 24–30°C (75–86°F) during the day. Nights are mild, averaging 20–24°C (68–75°F). In winter (December to February), daytime temperatures are typically 20–23°C (68–73°F), with nighttime temperatures around 15–17°C (59–63°F).
